Question for Astound: How do Astound define 'team' and 'project'? Provide 2-3 concrete examples from Core/Commerce expressed as a data structure: does a user belong to one team or many; does a project grant access or is it only a reporting label; how do Hub, team and project nest under an organization?
Why it matters / what it blocks: Blocks per-team/project analytics drill-down, budgets, hard cutoffs, and rate limits. Hub is agreed as a geographic grouping; team/project are the missing layers beneath it.
Options & our recommendation: Recommend: user belongs to exactly one team (like organization today, keeps queries and authz simple); project as a request-level label for reporting only, not entitlement. Once examples land we design the schema against them (~1-2 wks to implement the dimension end to end).

Topic: Identity source of truth + external platform mapping
Question for Astound: What is the authoritative identity provider going forward - Salesforce, Okta, Entra, GitHub? And which external platforms hold user activity we must correlate (which Git host counts as the SCM of record), with what API access, and what is the mapping rule from an external identity (e.g. commit-author email, SCM login) to a platform user?
Why it matters / what it blocks: Blocks full commit analytics (commits outside Claude Code are invisible today), automated offboarding beyond Salesforce, and any IDE/SCM productivity correlation. Only Salesforce SSO is wired today, including automatic deprovisioning.
Options & our recommendation: Recommend: keep Salesforce as IdP if that is the corporate directory (offboarding reconciliation already live); if Okta/Entra is the real directory, say so now - that is a new connector and re-opens SCIM as the right channel. For SCM: name one host + grant webhook/API access; verified-email mapping to platform users, with a manual override table for mismatches (~1 wk after the decision).

Topic: Safety policy - what 'safety' means for Astound
Question for Astound: Confirm the category list and, per category, block vs audit-only. Is PHI (health data) in scope? Is toxicity/brand-risk classification required (that needs a classifier, not pattern heuristics)? Should in-flight redaction (rewrite before forwarding) replace blocking for any category?
Why it matters / what it blocks: The scanners are live with our defaults: BLOCK jailbreak, credit cards, SSNs on ingress; secrets and SSNs on buffered egress; email/phone audit-only. Until Astound signs this off, enforcement reflects our judgement, not their policy.
Options & our recommendation: Recommend: ratify the current block list as v1; add PHI only if regulated health data actually transits the gateway; treat toxicity/brand-risk as a phase-2 item needing a model-based classifier (separate estimate). Redaction-instead-of-block is a scoped design item, not a toggle.

Question for Astound: Review the live first-pass quotas against expected traffic: 600 requests + $20 per user per hour; $200 per organization per day (runaway backstop above the monthly plan budgets). What numbers do you want?
Why it matters / what it blocks: Too tight throttles legitimate work; too loose defeats the runaway-agent backstop. Only Astound knows expected per-seat intensity.
Options & our recommendation: Recommend: run 2 weeks of real traffic, then set user/hour at ~3x observed p95 and org/day at ~2x observed peak day. We can produce the observed numbers from the dashboard on request.

Question for Astound: Define what 'quality' means: an agreed eval set of representative tasks (with expected outcomes or a grading rubric) against which providers/models can be scored.
Why it matters / what it blocks: Blocks quality-normalized provider cost comparison and any automatic optimal-model routing. Cost/latency sides are already measured; quality has no data source without this.
Options & our recommendation: Recommend: start with 20-50 real tasks from Core/Commerce workloads, graded pass/fail; we run them per provider/model and join the scores to the existing cost/latency telemetry. Decide later whether routing recommendations live in the gateway or an eval layer.

Question for Astound: Name the target stack: Datadog, Splunk, or LGTM (Grafana). Provide the ingestion endpoint + credentials for the chosen one.
Why it matters / what it blocks: OTLP ingest and the live audit stream exist; nothing pushes to an external SIEM/APM yet. Building all three exporters unprompted is waste.
Options & our recommendation: Recommend: whichever the on-call team already lives in. Datadog/LGTM = OTLP exporter (~1-2 wks); Splunk = HEC JSON push (~1 wk).

Topic: Compliance regime for the audit trail
Question for Astound: Which standard must the audit trail satisfy (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR-only, sector-specific)? And what retention window is required for ai_requests?
Why it matters / what it blocks: The trail is complete but append-only by convention, not mechanism, and currently unbounded. The regime picks the hardening: DB-role REVOKE (cheap), hash-chaining, or WORM export - and the retention sweep we must add.
Options & our recommendation: Recommend: DB-role REVOKE UPDATE/DELETE + a defined retention window covers SOC 2/ISO in practice (~1 wk); hash-chaining or WORM only if an auditor explicitly requires tamper-evidence.

Question for Astound: What are you actually trying to achieve per key? Individual USER budgets are already enforced (per-user hourly dollar/request quotas; every key inherits its owner's limits; org caps above). Do you have a case where ONE identity needs MULTIPLE keys with different budget/rate/model policy per key?
Why it matters / what it blocks: Determines adapt vs build. If each application/customer gets its own platform account, per-user enforcement already gives per-app budgets and the requirement is met as-is. Many-keys-per-identity policy is a ~2-week core change.
Options & our recommendation: Recommend: send the concrete scenarios (which systems hold keys, what limits each needs). Default position: model each app/consumer as its own account and close the row without new build.
